_what_this_is: Focused regression probes for the native pull-request authority runtime.
Each probe is applied only to a copied repository sandbox and must make the focused suite go red.

defects.why: The PR checkout token could remain in Git config for later checkout subprocesses.
The code-fetching action could drift between validations without review.
The Python setup action could drift between validations without review.
The native authority could silently move to a new Python patch release.
The uv setup action could drift between validations without review.
The native authority could silently use a different dependency resolver than the validated worker.
The Bun setup action could drift between validations without review.
The native authority could silently move to a different Bun runtime.
A pull_request trigger executes the PR's copy of this workflow; the PR could edit its judge.
The guard would be loaded from the PR head instead of the protected base tip.
The guard would run in head mode and the workflow would stop asserting base anchoring.

defects.find:
permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
      issues: read
defects.replace:
permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
      issues: read
defects.why: The judging job would hold write authority it does not need.
Auto-merge would be armed without the expected head, so a head the authority never judged could merge.
Auto-merge would be armed for autonomous PRs and for PRs the authority refused.
The merge job would no longer refuse when the judged head and the event head disagree.
The SDK would request /api/v1/v1/messages again and every model call would fail as it did on the first canary dispatch.

defects.find:
echo "FACTORY_PREFLIGHT_REFUSED worker CLI cannot reach model $model"
              head -c 600 /tmp/route-probe.json; echo; head -c 400 /tmp/route-probe.err; echo
              exit 1
defects.replace:
echo "FACTORY_PREFLIGHT_REFUSED worker CLI cannot reach model $model"
              head -c 600 /tmp/route-probe.json; echo; head -c 400 /tmp/route-probe.err; echo
              true
defects.why: A dead model route would be logged and the dispatch would proceed to burn a validation ladder discovering it.
The raw probe would again prove a different request than the one the worker makes.

defects.find: required_labels="$(python3 -c 'import json; from factory_kernel.triage import label_vocabulary; print("\n".join(label_vocabulary(json.load(open(".factory/kernel.json"))["labels"])))')"
defects.replace: required_labels="factory:accepted factory:rejected factory:rate-limited factory:in-progress factory:needs-review factory:needs-fix factory:needs-human factory:stop"
defects.why: The preflight would again check a hand-typed subset, and triage would crash on the first priority:* or type:* label the repository lacks.
The daily regression would run static+unit only and report main green without the browser journey, holdouts or mutations.
A harness that exited zero without emitting the full-gate marker would be reported as a pass.
A draft PR would attempt to arm auto-merge, which GitHub refuses, turning the optional job red for a correct outcome (observed on #50).
A branch with commits pushed after its merged PR would be deleted with the unmerged work on it; only a tip that is exactly the merged PR head may go.
The regression job would bypass triage by accepting its own issue.

defects.find:
if [ "$state" = "dirty" ]; then
            echo "TRUST_ROOT_REFUSED pr is not mergeable (conflicting with base); rebase"
            exit 1
          fi
defects.why: A conflicting maintainer PR would again sit silently with one green required check and no quick gate.

defects.find:
echo "TRUST_ROOT_REFUSED pr is not mergeable (conflicting with base); rebase"
            exit 1
defects.replace: echo "TRUST_ROOT_REFUSED pr is not mergeable (conflicting with base); rebase"
defects.why: The refusal would be printed but the required check would stay green, so the ruleset would learn nothing.
A branch with no merged PR at all (an open PR, or work never proposed) would be deleted.

defects.find:
- name: Upload run transcripts and artifacts (observability)
        if: always()
defects.replace:
- name: Upload run transcripts and artifacts (observability)
        if: false
defects.why: Observability, not authority: without the upload no per-stage timing or transcript survives the runner, and a slow or failed stage cannot be read after the fact.

defects.find:
echo "FACTORY_PREFLIGHT_REFUSED GitHub Actions may not create pull requests (Settings > Actions > General > Workflow permissions)"
              exit 1
defects.replace: echo "FACTORY_PREFLIGHT_REFUSED GitHub Actions may not create pull requests (Settings > Actions > General > Workflow permissions)"
defects.why: An explicit 'Actions may not create pull requests' would be printed and ignored; the run would spend a full build before failing at gh pr create, exactly the two hours the fifth canary defect cost.

defects.find:
- name: Dispatch exactly one factory action
        if: inputs.resume_pr == '' && inputs.resume_run_id == ''
defects.replace: - name: Dispatch exactly one factory action
defects.why: The ordinary dispatch would lose its inverse guard and run after a resume too, so one worker run could finish one PR and start another build; the run must take exactly one action.
